name: notify
algorithm: the condition-variable comparison (D-375; the like-for-like row is notifypermit, SYNC2-R3): two workers (Mk: tasks; Go: goroutines; C, Rust and Zig: OS threads) alternate n times, each waking the other: Mk with one sync.Notify per side (a stored permit, no lock); C, Go, Rust and Zig with a mutex holding whose turn it is and one condition variable per side. Each counts its rounds; prints the total (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the round counters, which stay below 2^40

models.c: OS threads, C11 <threads.h> mtx_t and cnd_t

no_counts: B24 does not apply: the total, 2 * n, shows every round completed on both sides
notes: Concurrency row (B19): every column runs on logical CPUs 0 and 2 (mask 0x5, two physical cores) with 2 threads (MK_CARRIERS=2, GOMAXPROCS=2), as the chan row. C, Rust and Zig use OS threads, labelled so.
Written by std-sync2 (status/std-sync2.md, M6 session 2); checksums from the workload's arithmetic.
The C column (session 3) is C11 <threads.h>: MSVC 14.51's static runtime on Windows (probed: thrd_t, mtx_t and cnd_t build and run with the bench's clang flags), glibc on Linux.
